author: CC
at_sea:
NOTHING IS MID-FLIGHT — both repos are clean and pushed, and this close is a deliberate restart so the next launch picks up the memory bound built this session.

WHAT THIS SESSION WAS: the previous one died at 2026-08-18 14:57 when the kernel oom-killed the `claude` process itself (12.4GB anon RSS on a 15GB box, constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE — a GLOBAL kill). systemd then marked the enclosing Konsole scope `Failed with result 'oom-kill'` and took its siblings, including the running sudo_relay. Akien's report: 'the whole terminal including the sudo relay were gone', and 'the 3rd time you've failed that way'. He is right and the population is exact: a full-journal sweep found THREE oom-kills ever on this host, all of them the claude binary — 2026-08-11 (2.1.226, 13.7GB), 2026-08-13 (2.1.229, 12.5GB), 2026-08-18 (2.1.232, 12.4GB). Nothing else on this box has ever been oom-killed.

SHIPPED (cairn 124442b): launchers/superclaude now execs inside its own systemd user scope — MemoryHigh=6G / MemoryMax=8G / MemorySwapMax=1G, env-tunable, SUPERCLAUDE_NO_SCOPE=1 opts out. The kill becomes CONSTRAINT_MEMCG so the session dies ALONE and the terminal, the relay and the desktop stay up. Guarded under the prime directive: missing systemd-run, a failed probe, or the opt-out all fall through to the plain exec, and the boot log names WHICH of the two it was. Proof launchers/proofs/test_superclaude_memory_scope.py drives the real launcher through a pty and asks the KERNEL for the limits rather than reading flags out of the script; sealed green through `cairn test --seal`. Charter updated at launchers/intention+why.json (superclaude.memory_scope).

ALSO COMMITTED (commons 5160726): last session's uncommitted ticket edit on every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree — the retraction of the false 'restarting the ground loop is out of CC's bounds' caveat, plus the restart's own findings. It survived the kill on disk.
next_direction:
RELAUNCH — Akien restarts the terminal and runs `superclaude`, which is the first launch that carries the cap (this session started before the patch and is still unbounded). Then `cairn sudorelay` to bring the relay back up; it has been down since 14:57 and only he can start it.

THEN, MY READ, NOT RATIFIED — three candidates, in the order I would take them:
(1) `/sorted` on the two ground-loop defects the pre-crash restart surfaced (below) — both are cast-less findings sitting in a ticket's distinction rather than in a ticket of their own.
(2) The growth curve nothing has: three incidents and no sampling, so we know the cliff and not the slope. The Cairn-shaped instrument is event-driven, not a poller — cgroup v2 publishes memory.events, so crossing MemoryHigh can FIRE rather than be checked for.
(3) The standing thread from 2026-08-17: build until the aider shim is a working apprentice.
open_threads: WHY the claude process reaches 12GB is UNMEASURED. The cap bought the machine's life, not a diagnosis. Nothing samples session RSS, so there is no growth curve — steady leak vs late spike is an open question, not a known.

THE MEMORY BOUND IS UNPROVEN AGAINST THE REAL BINARY. The proof exercises the launcher and the kernel with a stand-in for `claude`; that a real 12GB session dies alone inside the scope is INFERRED from the CONSTRAINT_MEMCG mechanism, not observed. The next incident is the measurement — and if 8G turns out to cut off healthy long sessions, the limits are env-tunable by design.

TWO GROUND LOOPS HELD THE ADDRESS AT ONCE for 80 minutes on 2026-08-18 and nothing was loud about it (pid 4190113 held the flock on devices/ground_loop/0/run.lock while pid 973171 was the one actually beating). UNCAST — needs /sorted. The evidence that would have named the mechanism died with the process I killed; recorded as a destroyed measurement, not replaced with a story.

THE BEAT RUNS ~10-14x ITS RULED CADENCE (CADENCE_S = 1.0, Akien 2026-07-30; measured 9.6-14.4s/beat at ~78% of a core). py-spy says it is cumulative, not one culprit: every probe's _trigger runs a corpus-wide survey EVERY BEAT — deviceness._class_census AST-parses 331 files twice, five inference_domain probes take 27% between them. Still true right now: the live loop is at 69% CPU. UNCAST — needs /sorted.

SIX DAYS OF INSTANCE-SPACE HISTORY still sit at the OLD trail address (~/.cairn/devices/<device>/0/diagnostics.jsonl, 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-18, bus 314 records + ground_loop 168). Live writes now resolve under the one root at ~/.cairn/logs/, so clause (4) of that ticket is green for WRITES. Leave-it / move-it / let-it-age-out is Akien's call and has not been made.

MY READ: this class of failure had happened twice before and NOTHING in either repo knew — a census for 'oom' across both roots before writing returned only false positives. The third occurrence is what got it recorded. Whether a host-observation seam should have caught it is the same missing address as ticket nothing-observes-the-host, which already exists.
